rationale: Sulpiride (selective D2/D3 + some D4; minimal anticholinergic activity; renally excreted; high prolactin) to olanzapine (multi-receptor SGA; high metabolic risk; strong H1/M1 activity). Sulpiride is sometimes used in ASEAN region for negative symptoms (low doses 200–400 mg) or as cost-effective antipsychotic. Common reason for switch: insufficient efficacy, metabolic acceptance of olanzapine for better tolerability of EPS, or formulary. Sulpiride has minimal anticholinergic activity, so cross-taper can proceed at a standard pace without significant cholinergic rebound. Metabolic monitoring is essential as metabolic risk increases significantly on olanzapine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start olanzapine 5 mg nocte. Continue sulpiride 800 mg. Record baseline weight, fasting glucose, fasting lipids before starting olanzapine.
Increase olanzapine to 10 mg nocte (target). Plateau sulpiride. Allow olanzapine to approach steady state.
Reduce sulpiride to 400 mg. Prolactin levels fall as sulpiride is reduced — warn female patients about possible menstrual changes.
Reduce sulpiride to 200 mg. Olanzapine at steady state. Sedation and weight increase likely.
Stop sulpiride. Continue olanzapine 10 mg nocte. Metabolic monitoring at 4 and 12 weeks. Dietary counselling for weight management.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sulpiride 800 mg ≈ olanzapine 10 mg (DDD-equivalence: sulpiride 800 mg/day ≈ olanzapine 10 mg/day; Maudsley 15th CPZ-equivalence: sulpiride 200 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ olanzapine 2.5 mg). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
